items.title: 6 Upcoming 7 Seaters From Hyundai And Kia: Hyundai Palisade To Kia Carnival Hybrid
points: Kia has launched its first strong-hybrid SUV, the Sorento, in the Indian market.
With rising demand for seven-seaters, Kia as well as Hyundai have plans to introduce more models in this segment.
The Carnival Hybrid is based on the same Limousine Plus trim as the existing model, which means it is expected to retain the premium features available in the current top-spec variant.
The MPV will be powered by the same 1.6-litre turbo-petrol engine used in the Sorento Hybrid.
In the Sorento, this engine produces 180 PS and 265 Nm of torque.
However, the electric motor in the Carnival Hybrid is slightly more powerful than the unit used in the Sorento, producing 73.4 PS and 304 Nm of torque.
This MPV will use a 1.5-litre naturally aspirated petrol strong-hybrid engine that we will see in the Seltos and the upcoming Hyundai Creta next year.
The Hyundai Alcazar currently comes with a 1.5-litre turbo-petrol and a 1.5-litre turbo-diesel engine, with manual, 6-speed DCT, and automatic transmission options.

items.title: Delhi breathes worst air on Diwali eve in 10 years
points: Delhi wakes up to Diwali on Sunday after its most polluted festival eve in a decade, with a perfect storm gathering over the night to come.

Farm fires in Punjab and Haryana climbed to their highest this season on Saturday — and the Isro satellite’s count rose for a 10th straight day, the ground wind fell calm after sunset, and within two hours of the first evening window for firecrackers…
The 4pm air quality index (AQI) on Saturday was 369, “very poor” on the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) 0-500 scale and the highest for the day before Diwali since 2016, when it was 404.

items.title: A bridge between past and present
points: Pathak belongs to Muzaffarpur in Bihar, and is looking at some coins from the Mauryan (321–185 B.C.E) and Gupta ages (early 4th to mid-6th Century C.E.).
She passes through interactive galleries which highlight Bihar’s pivotal role in shaping two major world religions: Jainism and Buddhism.
“I have been thinking of coming here for a long time, but after reading on social media that the museum is ranked the best in Asia, I decided to spend a day here,” she says.
Pathak is enroute to Muzaffarpur for the Deepavali holidays and came to the museum directly from Patna’s Jay Prakash Narayan airport, about four kilometres away.
Pathak is proud of her State that is often in the news for poverty and violence.

items.title: Ahead of Deepavali, Chhath festivals, migrants reach Bihar in hordes covering thousands of kilometers
points: Ahead of Deepavali and the four-day Chhath festival, migrants are visiting different places of Bihar in hordes.
With the flight fares skyrocketing and train ticket charts shown full, migrants are reaching their destination by buses and even riding on old auto-rickshaws covering thousands of kilometres.

Four young men on Saturday (November 7, 2026), from Bengaluru, travelled about 2,200 km riding on an old auto-rickshaw to reach Areraj town, near Someshwarnath Dham temple in Motihari of East Champaran district in Bihar.

Reaching their destination in three days, they told local media persons that it was their “desire to celebrate Deepavali and Chhath festival along with family members” and the air ticket fares had gone beyond their capacity.
In view of these two major festivals all the leaves for police officials have been cancelled till November 17, a senior official said.
The Chhath festival this year begins on November 13 and will continue till November 16.

items.title: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav writes to President, seeks action against DU Professor Sangeet Ragi
points: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav wrote a letter to President Draupadi Murmu, requesting her to order strict action against Delhi University Professor Sangeet Ragi for allegedly insulting the Yadav community.
Mr. Yadav said that he used the abusive language on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

He mentioned that action is necessary so that it serves as an exemplary punishment, ensuring that in a diverse country like India, no one dares to insult any society, class or community in the name of freedom of expression, and thus hurting unity and…
The three-page letter dated November 6, 2026, was shared with media on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

“I am writing to you in my capacity as a Member of Parliament (Rajyasabha) to express my serious concern regarding the alleged caste-based derogatory remarks made by Professor Sangeet Ragi of the University of Delhi against India’s largest community…

items.title: US Military Says It Disabled Cargo Vessel In Gulf Of Oman
points: Smoke rises from a burning vessel, following what the US Central Command said was a strike on an Iranian-affiliated dhow, at a location given as the Gulf of Oman, in this still image taken from a handout video released October 14, 2026.

US Central Command/Handout via REUTERS Nov 7 (Reuters) – An American military aircraft fired on and disabled a commercial vessel that tried to break the US blockade of Iran on Saturday, US Central Command said.

The St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port, and a US plane fired precision munitions at its stern after US forces directed the crew to abandon targeted spaces, Central Command said.
Central Command estimated that its naval blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil.
US President Donald Trump has been threatening to carry out a new offensive against Iran.

points: The agitation at the Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (SRFTI) continued for 42 days as class suspension was extended till December 11, affecting academic life.
Students of the film institute on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that “This Diwali we choose to resist”, while authorities said they were “keen" to resume classes.

“While the faculty and administration are ready to resume classes, a section of students continues to remain disengaged from academics and disrupt the functioning of the Institute through repeated violations of its rules and orders,” Registrar Deepak Kumar…
As of November 7, at least 25 students have received show cause notices, with 11 of them receiving them last Thursday (November 5, 2026).

items.title: Presidency University expels student for allegedly defacing Vivekananda poster
points: The Presidency University has expelled two students for allegedly defacing Swami Vivekananda posters inside the campus, official sources said.
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad had alleged that Left student factions had vandalised the poster and had filed a police complaint on October 14.
The university is not in a position to tolerate any abuse to any thinkers/ideas/organizations,” Presidency University registrar Debajyoti Konar said.
The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) condemned the expulsion on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Our message is clear: ABVP possesses the only vaccine capable of eliminating the Chinese virus of anti-national ideology,” Ananta Barui, State Media In-charge, ABVP told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

items.title: Locals burn effigy of Christian priests at Basanti in WB
points: A group of locals at Basanti in West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas on Thursday (November 5, 2026) burnt effigy of local Christian priests and submitted a memorandum to the police station against the local priests.
Basanti has been on the boil since November 1 after a newly constructed church was vandalised by a mob claiming their allegiance to a Hindutva outfit.

The protest on Thursday (November 5, 2026) was organised by Adivasi Eilya Parishad, a local organisation whose representatives said that Adivasis are being lured for conversion on the promise of curing disease, which should not be allowed.
The West Bengal chapter of National Christian Council (NCC) in a press statement added that effigy of local priests were set on fire at Chowmatha crossing in Basanti.
“Later in the evening, during the Friday prayer service, a group of approximately 20–25 people allegedly surrounded women attending the service.

items.title: Jumbo hustle: the transfer of elephants to Tamil Nadu’s temples
points: In temples, elephants may be used in rituals, processions and festival-related functions.
They may stand near the sanctum or participate in ceremonial occasions, and are often expected to interact with devotees.
Representational file image. | Photo Credit: M.

Srinath Nothing illustrates more poignantly the exalted status once enjoyed by temple elephants, and their subsequent fall, than the story of Kesavan — the elephant of the Adi Kesava Perumal Temple at Kanniyakumari’s Thiruvattar — who is the protagonist of…
A favourite of the King, even when he was a prince, Kesavan developed a sense of his own exceptional status.
Even his chief mahout was afraid to command him.
The mahout’s emaciated leg, a result of Kesavan’s fury, bears testimony to what the elephant was capable of.
The elephant, which once commanded fear and deference, would now meekly extend its leg to help the mahout climb on to its back.

items.title: A wet Deepavali ahead for many parts of Tamil Nadu
points: Nearly 20 north coastal and interior districts, including Chennai, would also receive moderate rainfall on Deepavali day. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B A wet Deepavali seems likely across Tamil Nadu on Sunday, with weather agencies predicting rain…

The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has forecast fairly widespread rainfall across Tamil Nadu, with intense spells expected in south and delta districts, while north coastal and interior districts are expected to get moderate rainfall.
According to the RMC, heavy rainfall may occur in isolated places of seven delta and south districts, including Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Ramanathapuram, and Thoothukudi, on Sunday.
Nearly 20 north coastal and interior districts, would also receive moderate rainfall on Deepavali day.
Wet weather is expected to prevail across the State till November 12, with heavy rainfall set to lash delta and southern districts till Tuesday.
While a low-pressure area is likely to develop over southeast Bay of Bengal around November 13, it has only a slim chance of intensifying further as a depression.

items.title: 301 Colony residents put forward 10 recommendations to foster tribal settlement’s development
points: The meeting took place on November 3 in the presence of the Adimaly Tribal Development Officer and the site in-charge of the Tribal Rehabilitation and Development Mission (TRDM).

Additionally, the meeting urged the Scheduled Tribes Development department to deliver essential amenities, including electricity, paved roads, drinking water, walkways, and retaining walls, as well as to renovate dilapidated houses through relevant…
The Tribal Development Officer stated that registration procedures would begin by electing a 15-member committee of beneficiaries.

The Tribal Development Officer reiterated that all individuals who leased out allotted plots must reclaim the land, cultivate it, and establish permanent residence, warning that non-compliance would result in deed cancellations and reallotments.
According to officials, 211 of the 301 families have already settled in the colony.
The remaining 90 families have been unable to construct homes due to various hardships, including deaths in the family.
Antony government allotted one acre of land each to 301 tribal families.

items.title: Keralam measles outbreaks call for a relook at disease epidemiology
points: As of November 6, the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme had reported 824 confirmed and 1,681 probable measles cases in the State.
A second dose, at 18 months, was introduced in 2010 to address immunity gaps following the first dose and support measles elimination.

Following major measles outbreaks in Mumbai in 2023, when more than 31% of reported cases were among infants below nine months, a seroprevalence study found that only 66.8% of mothers had adequate measles antibodies to protect their infants.

A World Health Organisation (WHO) informal technical consultation report, published in Vaccine in May 2025, acknowledged that women acquiring immunity through vaccination rather than natural infection might transfer lower levels of measles antibodies to…

A study by the Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology (RGCB), involving 684 children aged four to 18 from Keralam and Tamil Nadu, who had received at least two doses of a measles-containing vaccine, assessed their measles antibody levels.
